rulings: Ruling: execute inline on a separate branch in the existing checkout — the user requested all work and memory/disk conservation, and the tracked tree was clean — branch isolation does not isolate concurrent untracked files, so stage explicit paths only.

Ruling: proceed with the approved four-item scope and the written design without another scope-confirmation round — the user said to process all four and has repeatedly requested uninterrupted progress — record consequential implementation decisions and preserve all stated invariants.

Task 1 Ruling: descriptor/catalog replacements rebuild descriptor ownership and reconcile equal model records — type ID renumbering and cross-model overlays require complete semantics — costs a full descriptor rebuild on an actual global catalog change, while unchanged publications do no conversion/rebuild.

Task 1 Ruling: comparisons against archived adoption controls normalize absent versus undefined health keys and apply current project source attachments in the fresh oracle — the older baseline predates pythonPath decoration and project contexts — preserve actual non-undefined health/content checks.

Task 2 Ruling: retain fresh before/after/adoption source walks and stat every file, but pass previous snapshots to reuse verified Path/entry/hash allocations — directory timestamp shortcuts would miss nested additions or restored mtimes — less theoretical speedup, stronger correctness.

Task 2 Ruling: seed coverage is its actual parsed/unparseable/shadowed files rather than the wider dependency proof scope — a proof can cover sibling sources that were never in this static index — additional imports may require a source rebuild.

Task 3 Ruling: detached summaries use immutable tuple collections and frozen dictionary rows; ordinary live-registry records outside the coordinator keep their existing behavior — sharing mutable lists/maps would cross profile edits — code that tries to mutate published detached leaves now receives TypeError and must create a replacement.

Task 4 Ruling: observe file reads, existence checks and import directories inside the owned worker; keep only path identities, never configuration values — missing configuration additions and external dependency replacements must invalidate caches — unobservable time/network-dependent settings are not proven equivalent by file witnesses.

Task 4 Ruling: cache at most 64 settings profiles in fixed slots, 128 MiB per artifact and 512 MiB total per workspace; excess profiles still run normally — bounded cache data must not reduce registry coverage — very large inputs may deliberately remain cold.

Task 4 Ruling: reuse existing spooled static serialization with a workspace-owned output path and validated producer marker — nested-project seeds must be removed by the existing workspace cache-clear command — a missing/changed marker rebuilds the static seed.

Final Ruling: carry unchanged independent profiles with a stable interpreter/code/environment/roster context plus each profile own exact dependency source proof — do not relabel old records with a new global source fingerprint — extra unrelated source changes need not force unaffected registries, while additions/aliases/config/dependency changes still validate their witnesses.

Final Ruling: retry a witnessed dependency race once serially within the remaining original per-profile runtime budget; distinguish unsupported observations from changed inputs — a settled dependency should recover without manual retries — repeated races degrade visibly instead of publishing the raced result.

Final Ruling: arbitrary time/network-dependent settings remain outside file-witness equivalence, as the reviewer declined to judge this documented boundary — no claim of a proof for external mutable services — explicit cache clearing or a visible input change may be necessary when only those services change.

Final Ruling: report the pre-existing static inheritance/import-switch failure separately instead of expanding this four-optimization release into an unrelated static-index repair — the plan explicitly permits reporting pre-existing failures — that existing incorrect inherited-field case remains outside this change.

Task 5 Ruling: do not execute the default vscode-test launcher because its dependencies add --no-sandbox, --disable-gpu-sandbox and --disable-workspace-trust — user explicitly forbids security weakening — use an explicit editor test launch retaining default protections and the previously approved synthetic fixture folder, or report that gate unavailable.

Task5 Ruling: reuse a separate already-installed official VS Code test application for CUA targeting instead of disturbing the user main Code process or copying another application — identical bundle IDs prevented targeting separate instances of the main installation — reported host version is1.143.1, and its current Python/Pylance extensions were activated.

Final Ruling: follow the explicit existing commit/push/release authorization instead of presenting the finishing skill integration menu again — main fork point and current remote both c5ef62c; no integration ambiguity — only fast-forward integration, preserving unrelated files.

Final Ruling: retain the plan explicit exception for the independently reproduced pre-existing full-suite failure instead of the finishing skill generic stop-on-any-failure rule — all changed-path gates pass and both full runs report the identical baseline failure — release notes/audit must not claim an entirely green full suite.

Final Ruling: publish a new immutable0.2.2032 release for the deferred-startup fix, retaining public0.2.2031 and its benchmark provenance — the already published artifact must not be silently replaced — repeat the changed-path Django5/6 regression and package/publication integrity gates, while retaining the original full-suite/editor evidence under0.2.2031.
